method: The page sizes a lampshade cover from the frame. Each panel is treated as a trapezoid whose bottom edge is the bottom ring circumference (pi times the bottom diameter) and whose top edge is the top ring circumference, with a panel height equal to the slant height plus an edge allowance at the top and bottom. The slant height is the straight shade height for a drum shade, or the square root of the height squared plus half the difference between the bottom and top diameters squared for an empire shade, which is the true distance between the rings along the fabric. Because fabric comes in fixed usable widths, the page takes the smallest whole number of equal panels, from one to eight, whose width including a seam allowance at both sides fits the usable width, then lays those panels across the fabric and reports how many lengths down the bolt the cover needs. Seam and edge allowances are entered by the user: one seam allowance is added at each side of every panel and one edge allowance at the top and at the bottom. Lining is assumed to take the same length as the cover. A pattern repeat, nap or directional print, print matching across the seams, fabric shrinkage, bias stretch and any trimming or straightening of the cut edges are not modelled, so the figure is a minimum to buy rather than a guaranteed cut.
